title: Unpredictable what actually will be pasted due to copy-only-selection item not being visually differentiated in any way
line: The clipboard popup now marks which entry Ctrl+V pastes and which one middle-click pastes.
explanation: With 'Text selected with the pointer' saved in history and not kept in sync with the clipboard, the clipboard and the selection hold different entries, but Klipper only knew the history order, so the popup showed both entries the same way and the top one was often the selection, not what Ctrl+V pastes. The change (Tomáš Hnyk's draft MR !6887) makes the history model remember which entry each buffer holds and exposes it as two roles; the popup shows a paste icon on the clipboard entry and a mouse icon on the selection entry, only when the two buffers are tracked separately.

commits.message:
klipper: Mark which entry is in the clipboard and which in the selection

With the selection saved in history and not synced, nothing showed which
entry Ctrl+V and which middle-click would paste. Klipper now tracks both
buffers and the popup marks each with an icon and a tooltip.

BUG: 355841

media.caption: 'first' copied with Ctrl+Shift+C, 'second' only selected: both entries look alike and the highlighted top one is the selection
Same steps: 'second' has the mouse icon (middle-click), 'first' the paste icon (Ctrl+V)
